title: Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV) Technician (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS, DC I&L #
raw_text:
6. MOS 2143, Amphibious Combat Vehicle (ACV) Technician (GySgt to Pvt) PMOS,
DC I&L #

    a. Summary. The ACV Technician performs basic automotive duties
including the inspection, maintenance, and repair of the ACV family of
vehicles. The ACV Technician performs basic shop administrative actions
utilizing technical manuals and automated information systems. The ACV
Technician can also operate the ACV FOV in support of combat and/or garrison
operations. The ACV Technician will perform operator and field-level
maintenance and maintain/manage associated tools and equipment, of which
licensed to operate. Accordingly, they will employ land navigation
techniques and must be knowledgeable with the operation of radios and weapon
systems when mounted on the vehicle during tactical operations. The Gunnery
Sergeant to corporal level supervises, and performs various duties incident
to the inspection, maintenance, and repair of the automotive and RWS/Turret
systems of the ACV. In addition, ACV Technicians prepare, maintain, and
supervise shop maintenance and management programs, and coordinate
maintenance and recovery operations according to grade and position.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must possess an MM score of 105 or higher.

            (2) Must have WS-B water survival qualification.

        (3) Must have normal vision to include color, acuity, field of vision
and depth perception. The examinee will not be disqualified for a vehicle
operator license because of color blindness or depth perception. However, if
color blindness or depth perception is indicated, he or she will be given


                                         3-143                        Enclosure (1)
 3120                                                                NAVMC 1200.1L



additional training, which will enable him or her to drive safely.         Must have
normal color vision.

        (4) Must meet initial strength test standards associated with PEF
assignments as listed in the glossary (pg. xiv) prior to shipping to recruit
training.

        (5) Must meet MOS classification standards as listed in the glossary
(pg. xiv) prior to graduating from recruit training.

        (6) No more than one yes in the blocks contained in section 6 on the
physical fitness inquiry for motor vehicle operators form (OF-345) is
acceptable.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Complete the Amphibious Combat Vehicle Basic Repairer Course
(M10AH33), Camp Pendleton, CA.

        (2) Complete the Amphibious Combat Vehicle Field Level Maintenance
New Equipment Training 2.0, licensed by the program manager.

        (3) Entry level and lateral move Marines must complete the Amphibious
Combat Vehicle Technician Course for assignment as a primary MOS.

        (4) Must complete the submerged vehicle egress trainer (SVET)
qualifications prior to completion of the Amphibious Combat Vehicle
Technician Course.

    d. Duties. For a complete listing of duties and tasks, refer to
reference, NAVMC 3500.2D.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Bus and Truck Mechanics and Diesel Engine Specialists 49-3031.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   Engineer Equipment Mechanic, 1341.

# For Marines that are trained on an amphibious combat vehicle in the legacy
field level maintenance new equipment training are required to complete the
evaluation program signed off on by the officer in charge of the training
transition unit in order to be awarded the 2143 PMOS.
common_text: The Ground Ordnance Maintenance OccFld maintains the serviceability of ground ordnance materials. Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units. Qualifications required include basic ordnance administration and knowledge; the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures. Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment. Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods. Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer. Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 2100, Basic Ground Ordnance Maintenance Marine. Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.

The Ground Ordnance Maintenance OccFld maintains the serviceability of ground ordnance materials. Duties include the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems possessed by Marine Corps units. Qualifications required include basic ordnance administration and knowledge; the capability to technically inspect/ analyze ordnance items and repair/fabricate the same, and to understand and implement operational repair facility procedures. Ground Ordnance maintainers impart technical knowledge onto organizational personnel, crews, and supervisors for proper corrective and preventive maintenance, inspection, and application of weapons and optical systems and all associated support equipment. Ground Ordnance Maintenance personnel are required to learn ground ordnance maintenance administrative procedures, repair analysis, technical inspection procedures, repair procedures, testing of ordnance equipment, and quality control methods. Entry level Occupations include Small Arms Repairer/Technician, Precision Weapons Repairer/Technician, Towed Artillery Systems Technician, Assault Amphibious Vehicle (AAV)/Assault Combat Vehicle (ACV) Repairer/Technician, Heavy Ordnance Vehicle Repairer/ Technician, Light Armored Vehicle (LAV) Repairer/Technician, Machinist, and Electro-Optical Ordnance Repairer. Senior enlisted Marines within the MOS are tasked with overseeing the inspection, repair, and maintenance of ground ordnance weapons and optical systems. Marines entering this OccFld will receive MOS 2100, Basic Ground Ordnance Maintenance Marine. Marines within this occupation are familiar with associated warranties and contract logistics support options for ground ordnance equipment and able to execute processes and procedures as part of weapons and optics systems sustainment plans.

nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
